World Agroforestry sheet gives temp as one mean-annual range (14-36). pH 6.5-8 is for its 'most suitable' deep, well-drained, fertile alluvial-colluvial soil. Frost is harmful. Soil texture not stated in the sheet.

Temp extremes: sheet gives min 1-7 and max 34-47, widest used. pH not given as numbers (sheet says slightly acid). Soil: sandy to clayey, best moist sandy loam with good subsoil drainage. Does not tolerate waterlogging. Needs 4-8 month dry season; frost damage at altitude.
ECOCROP absolute texture: heavy, medium, light, wide, organic. Drought tolerant; susceptible to fire and grazing. World Agroforestry lists temp -4 to 45 and rain 500-4500.
Listed in ECOCROP as Acacia nilotica. Tolerates fire, drought, salinity (medium), and long periodic flooding. ECOCROP flags it can become a weed.

Very drought tolerant (withstands 8-11 dry months); tolerates wind and medium salinity. World Agroforestry sheet gives its natural-range rainfall as only 120-250 mm, so ECOCROP's 400-800 optimal is a growing-well range, not where it naturally occurs.

leaf_habit: usually evergreen (sheet also calls it deciduous)
notes: pH 6.5-7.0 is for fertile, neutral soil (loose, moist alluvial loam with good drainage), not a stated tolerance limit. Grows along rivers and dry water courses. Used for reclaiming saline/alkaline soils and ravines. Seedlings susceptible to fire, drought, frost.

SECONDARY sources, not ECOCROP or the World Agroforestry sheet itself. The leaflet quotes mean annual temp 2-46 and rain 550-1500 mm, up to 1200 m. TNAU gives normal rainfall 750-1875 mm and absolute min/max temps 1-8 and 41-48. Grows on a wide variety of soils, prefers sandy. No pH numbers found. Leaf habit left blank because sources disagree (evergreen vs dry-forest deciduous). Verify against the World Agroforestry sheet before relying on it.
ECOCROP absolute texture: heavy, medium, light, organic. Tolerates drought and wind. ECOCROP flags it can become a weed.

ECOCROP: grows on most soil types, best on deep well-drained sandy loam with assured moisture; also sandy soils and heavy swelling clays; waterlogging tolerated; medium salinity. Soil texture left blank because ECOCROP's texture field is empty.

Values from the World Agroforestry species sheet. Altitude up to 1520 m. Soil: wide variety, prefers deep alluvial sandy loam with good drainage, also grows on shallow soil and rock crevices. No pH given. Needs protection from livestock and fire when young. Large crown limits use in crop intercropping.

World Agroforestry sheet: grows in most soils but prefers well-drained deep alluvial soil. No pH or texture numbers in the sheet. Another source (not verified) quotes pH 4.5-8.7, so ask before using it.

Values from the World Agroforestry species sheet. Altitude 0-1200 m. Prefers moist, fertile, freely drained sandy loam; accepts acid, calcareous and laterite soils. Stunted on dry sandy or poor soil and does not thrive where drainage is poor. Light demander, moderately frost hardy. No pH numbers given.

Values from the World Agroforestry species sheet. Temperature -6 to 48 is the wide extreme range the sheet reports (shade temperatures in the Punjab), so it is not a narrow optimum. pH 5-8 is where it 'grows well' on swampy, alkaline or stony soils. Does best on rich, well-drained soil. Needs a long dry season to fruit. Altitude 0-1200 m.

Values from the World Agroforestry species sheet. pH 6-7 is where seedlings thrive best (rich loamy soil), not a tolerance limit. Grows on shallow gravelly sites, black cotton soil, clay loams, even saline or waterlogged soils. Very drought resistant and frost hardy. Altitude up to 1500 m. Resists browsing.

Values from the World Agroforestry species sheet. Rainfall: 'at least 500 mm' (no upper limit). pH: prefers neutral to slightly acidic; 8.5 is the highest it has been introduced on successfully, so only abs_max is filled. Does well in well-drained clay or clay loam; harmed by prolonged waterlogging. Drought tolerant, killed back by freezes. Altitude 0-1000 m.

Values from the World Agroforestry species sheet. Natural habitat is sandy coasts and dunes; soils are well-drained and coarse (sands and sand loams). Tolerates calcareous and slightly alkaline soil and salt spray; intolerant of prolonged waterlogging; not fire resistant. Altitude 0-1400 m. Nitrogen-fixing. No pH numbers given.
ECOCROP absolute texture: heavy, medium, light. Leaf habit not stated in the sheet. Grown as a fruit crop; a plantation tree, not a forest restoration species.

Values from the World Agroforestry species sheet. The sheet writes temperature as '7-13 to 37-48'; I read the inner values (13, 37) as typical and the outer (7, 48) as extremes. Best soil is sandy loam, neutral to slightly alkaline; also grows on laterite, black cotton soil and limestone. Tolerates salinity, drought and waterlogging. Altitude 0-1500 m.

Values from the World Agroforestry species sheet. Establishes well on fertile, well-drained loam but poorly on heavy clays, although it tolerates heavy, eroded, acid, alkaline and waterlogged soils (Gemini had entered 'heavy', which is misleading). Killed by even light fires; tolerates drought and some frost after year one. Altitude 0-1800 m. Leaf habit not stated for the species.

Values from the World Agroforestry species sheet. The sheet's ecology text gives temperature as 18-28.5; the biophysical limits give 18-29. Drought resistant, not frost hardy, tolerates moderate shade. Soil texture not stated.

Values from the World Agroforestry species sheet. Grows best on fertile, well-drained loam; has done reasonably well on poor soils. Found with teak in monsoon and dry deciduous forest. Light demander, fairly drought resistant, needs protection from grazing. Altitude 0-1000 m. No pH numbers given.

Values from the World Agroforestry species sheet. HILL SPECIES: altitude 1200-3500 m, cool northern slopes. Not suited to plains such as Bilaspur. Prefers sandy loam rich in organic carbon; avoids stiff, badly drained soil; stunted on shallow rocky soil. Seedlings are not drought tolerant. No pH numbers given.

Values from the World Agroforestry species sheet. Common on deep loams or clays containing lime and on black cotton soils; grows best on well-drained, deep, moist soil; shallow dry soil and poor drainage stunt it. Altitude 0-1500 m. Nitrogen-fixing. No pH numbers given.
